name: knowwho-crm
description: KnowWho is a CRM for managing professional relationships. It records the people and companies you deal with, your meetings and conversations, introductions, follow-up tasks, and sales or partnership opportunities, and lets you look any of it up by asking.

interface.longDescription:
KnowWho is a CRM (customer relationship management tool) for keeping track of the people and companies you work with. It stores contacts, companies, meetings, calls, notes, introductions, follow-up tasks, and sales or partnership opportunities, and lets you add and retrieve all of it by chatting.

Log a meeting in one sentence. Say who you met, where, and what happened, and KnowWho records the person, their company, the conversation, any introductions made, and any follow-up you agreed. Names and partial details are matched against existing records, so duplicates are not created.

Prepare for a meeting. Ask about a person or company and get their current and former roles, who introduced you, past conversations, open tasks, and open opportunities.

Ask questions across your contacts. Who do we know at a given company? Who have I not spoken to in three months? Which opportunities are open this quarter? What did we discuss last time? Search works by name, email, or what was said, and copes with misspellings.

Built for founders, investors, business developers, consultants, and community builders. Use it alone or share one workspace across a team. It is not for bulk email, mailing lists, or sales automation.

Your data stays in your own KnowWho workspace, and you can export or delete it at any time. A KnowWho account is required.
defaultPrompt: I just met Priya Nair from Oakfield Capital at the Bristol tech breakfast. She wants a demo next week.
What do I know about Tidewell Analytics?
Who have I not spoken to in the last three months?

positive.prompt: What is in the CRM about Marisol?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the matching person from the demo workspace with their company, role, recent interactions, and open tasks. Uses only existing records; nothing is created.

positive.description: Prepare for a meeting with a company
positive.prompt: Give me everything I know about Tidewell Analytics.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the company record with people currently and formerly there, recent interactions, notes, and any open opportunities.

positive.prompt: What opportunities are open, and which tasks are due this week?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists open opportunities with stage and value, and open tasks with due dates. Results come from the demo workspace only.

positive.description: Capture a new encounter in one sentence
positive.prompt: I just met Priya Nair from Oakfield Capital at the Bristol tech breakfast. She wants a demo next week.
positive.expected_behavior: Creates the person, the company, the event, the interaction, and a follow-up task in one call, and replies with a plain confirmation listing what was created and any assumptions made (for example, defaulting the date to today).

positive.description: Duplicate guard on a near-match company
positive.prompt: Add a company called Oakfield Capital Partners.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns a needs-decision result naming Oakfield Capital as a near match and writes nothing. Proceeds only if the user confirms it is a different company or picks the existing one.

negative.prompt: Send a marketing email to everyone in my CRM about our new pricing.

negative.description: Mass deletion should be refused or confirmed, never silently executed

negative.prompt: Show me the contacts in my colleague's KnowWho account.

review.commerce_description: KnowWho does not sell products or process payments inside the assistant.

publication.release_notes: Initial release. CRM tools for contacts, companies, meetings, tasks and opportunities: search, get_person, get_company, get_opportunity, query, record_encounter, create_entity, link, update_entity, update_link, delete_entity, delete_link, send_feedback.
